reason: Dust falling into the disk belongs at the young star’s dusty disk, which should begin the grain-gathering process.

choice.with: Young star with a dusty disk

expectation: The infalling dust will join the disk and make material available for grain collisions.

effect: The dust has settled into the disk, providing material for the grain-gathering goal.
reaction: The role of gas drag in settling the grains is interesting.
reason: Slowly meeting grains suggest a gentle collision that could let dust stick together.
expectation: The grains will stick together and begin forming larger rocky particles.

effect: Gentle collisions produced fragile clumps, but they are not yet rocky pebbles.
reaction: The contrast between sticking and destructive collisions is interesting.
reason: The clumps may have more than one useful next step, so checking their partners will help distinguish growth from a hard collision.
expectation: The inspection will reveal whether the clumps can grow further or collide with faster grains.

alternatives.reason: A fast collision might address the second goal, but I would first check the clumps' options.

effect: The fast collision shattered the clumps into smaller grains and completed the hard-collision goal.
reaction: I was surprised the inspection automatically triggered the collision.
reason: Ice-coated grains moving inward are likely to change in the warm inner disk, which may help produce rocky pebbles.
expectation: The ice will warm and leave rocky material in the inner disk.

effect: The warm disk removed the ice, leaving rocky grains available for the pebble goal.
reaction: The distinction between evaporated ice and vanished material is useful.
reason: The stripped grains are the clearest starting point for making rocky pebbles, but their next partner is not obvious.
expectation: The inspection will show how the rocky grains can gather or grow.

alternatives.reason: Gentle encounters might promote sticking, but their compatibility is uncertain.

effect: The inspection automatically combined the dry grains with slowly meeting grains, producing rocky pebbles and completing the final goal.
reaction: It was satisfying to see gentle collisions build pebbles, with the qualification that sticking alone cannot make planets.

mostWorthwhile.text: The final pebble formation connected ice loss with gentle grain growth, while distinguishing pebbles from planets.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial dust-settling step was straightforward setup and less engaging than the collision outcomes.

surprise.text: Inspecting the fluffy clumps automatically caused their only available collision, shattering them rather than merely listing options.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless, though the automatic collision during inspection was unexpected.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what processes can take the pebbles beyond the limits of simple sticking.
